intro: Every day the dice roll a premise and a dozen constraints, and the game has to honour all of them. Tonight's roll was seed 1773262177, and it rolled a ledger who can't say no. Here's how that became a night of knocking on the doors of Cobwell House.

rolls.value: a ledger who can't say no
rolls.became: The inventory ledger of Cobwell House. Its whole job is writing down where things went, and it can't say no, so for 140 years, whenever anyone asked to borrow a teacup, it said yes and wrote it down. In a house like Cobwell, "anyone" was mostly the dead. It can't say no to a dare either, which is how the game starts.
Collecting, the way a ledger means it: calling in loans. It knows exactly who has every cup, because it wrote every loan down. It just has to get them back.
The Cobwell service: 99 cups, one for every hook on the dresser. Every one you get back hangs there for good, and the dresser filling up is the meter.

Ghosts answer a knock, so the ledger knocks on their doors with its cover, in time with the music. A knock that lands on the beat counts, and one dead on it counts double. Every room's door has its own knock, and the Ballroom ghosts won't answer anything but shave-and-a-haircut.

A ledger column is two digits wide, so everything stays under 100: 99 cups, up to 99 ghosts, nothing in the shop over 99 knocks. While you're away nobody's holding the pen, so the knocks only fill the column to 99.
Cornelius dared the ledger to get every cup back on the dresser. He knew it couldn't say no.

Cornelius is the map: Cornelius Cobwell drew the house, drew himself into the cartouche, and stayed. He's cheerfully, confidently wrong (the Billiard Room is a lake, the Conservatory is a duck pond), and the ghosts can only walk where he says, so a trip only finds its room some of the time. Every wrong turn goes in the book: Cornelius owes 1 right turn. To correct him you post ghosts in a room, because a map can't pretend a room isn't there with people standing in it.

When every room is empty, eleven cups are still out, all lent to "C." on eleven different dates. The ledger shows Cornelius his page: hundreds of right turns, in red, five to a gate. A map's whole job is being right, so he pays. He redraws himself true and walks the ledger to the Cellar, the one room he never drew, where his cups have been all along. He kept them because people only knock when they want something back.
Cornelius, and the "C." in Entry No. 1 on the ledger's page: one cup, lent to C., 1887. It's on screen from the first second.
Twelve rooms on the map, each with its own knock, and corrections that need more ghosts every time (the Ballroom wants 99). The ghosts and the wallpaper hands carry on at half pace while you're away.

rolls.value: stacked currencies (A makes B, B makes C)
rolls.became: Knocks call ghosts, and ghosts fetch cups. Ghosts are also what you pay Cornelius with, so every correction sends your fetchers off to stand in a room for good.

rolls.value: sacrifice part of your progress to multiply the rest
rolls.became: "Say yes": the ghosts keep asking to borrow cups, and the ledger can't say no, only make them wait. Say yes and half the cups on the dresser go back out to the rooms, for credit that makes the ghosts walk and the hands knock faster for good. A ghost in your debt works very hard.

Every 25 ghosts, they organise and all walk twice as fast; every 25 wallpaper hands find a rhythm and all knock twice as hard. Posting ghosts on the map can drop you back under a milestone, so it's worth thinking about when.

rolls.value: one last purchase that costs everything
rolls.became: Balance the Books: a full column of knocks and a full column of ghosts, 99 of each. The ledger pays every ghost back and closes every account, then turns to the last page.
A comic page: inked panels with hard shadows, halftone wallpaper, caption boxes for the numbers, a speech balloon for Cornelius, and KNOCK! bursts. Lettered in Bangers and Comic Neue.
Plums and mauves for a candlelit hall, wine-red for the ledger's cover, mint for the ghosts, parchment for the map, and a pencil red for every correction.

Marimbas in E harmonic minor, building a figure one note at a time the way Philip Glass would, with that spooky major chord on B. It's also the beat you knock to: the markers follow the music's own clock. Upstairs a second marimba and vibes join, and at the top of the house the glockenspiel chimes like teacups. Every knock plays a marimba note in the same key.
Ghosts in sheets with name tags (HELLO, I OWE: 1 CUP), hands in the wallpaper, a saucer of milk that's empty every time you look, a portrait whose eyes follow the floor. Spooky, never scary.

outro: The ghosts still ask to borrow cups, and the ledger still says yes. These days Cornelius tells it exactly where each cup will be.
